newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell shuts Nigeria oil stations, no force majeure.
newsitem.headline: Shell shuts Nigeria oil stations, no force majeure.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Tuesday it had closed five oil flow stations in the southeast because of tribal fighting.
"Armed youths went to our Nembe creek fields on Sunday, disarmed the police on duty and asked us to shut down which we have done," a Shell spokesman told Reuters in Lagos.
He said the production of the five stations was 120,000 barrels per day but that no force majeure had been declared.
"Exports are continuing normally at the Bonny terminal. Nembe production is fed into the Bonny stream," he said.
The youth had so far not made any demands and Shell said it was not directly connected with the incident.
"It appears to be a continuation of the problems which led to our closure of the same fields in March," the spokesman said.
At the time the communities were protesting over their merger into one local government area.
Shell has had to close many stations at several points in the last two months over protests by some tribes over a recent restructuring of local government areas by the military government.
The communities in Nembe are Ijaw-speaking like those in the western division of Shell's operations around Warri oil town where many flow stations were closed for weeks.
According to Shell all the flow stations in the western division except Warri River, have been reopened.
